turns.text: Hello! How have you been lately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Working from home is great, but I never really stop working.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a common trap. What could be your end of the day ritual, something that tells your brain work is over?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just a minute, I have to answer my roommate. Please stay quiet until I return.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you look at these two invitation samples for a second?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure. Oh, the cream one is really pretty.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right? But the white one is half the price.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Honestly, nobody keeps the invitation. Go with the cheaper one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mom will notice though. Which font do you like better?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The curly one. The other looks like a business letter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, curly font, white card. Deal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, back to what you were saying.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: So anyway, the trip is in June.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey, I'm back. Sorry about that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure thing. Did you think of a way to mark the end of work?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe a short walk around the block at six.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect, a fake commute. It really helps your brain switch off.
